$comment: Cross-language conformance fixture for Set-Cookie parsing (issue #301). Read by BOTH the engine gtest suite (set_cookie_test.cpp, via VAYU_ENGINE_SOURCE_DIR) and the app's vitest suite (app/src/modules/request-builder/components/ResponseViewer/parse-set-cookie.conformance.test.ts). The engine parses for pm.response.cookies, the renderer for the response Cookies tab; both read the same header off the same response, so a case answered two ways is a user seeing one thing in the UI and asserting another in a script. Every case is a raw header value exactly as it reaches a client - the two documented corruptions (a comma inside Expires, `=` padding inside a base64 value) are the reason this parser is not a split.

cases.name: the comma inside Expires is not a cookie boundary
cases.header: id=a3fWa; Expires=Wed, 21 Oct 2015 07:28:00 GMT; Secure; HttpOnly

cases.name: a base64 value keeps its = padding
a base64 value keeps both = of its padding
multiple Set-Cookie headers arrive joined by a comma
joined cookies where the first carries an expiry comma
cases.header: a=1; Expires=Wed, 21 Oct 2015 07:28:00 GMT, b=2; HttpOnly

cases.name: joined cookies with no space after the comma
a comma inside a value is kept when no name= follows it
a cookie cleared by the server has an empty value
surrounding whitespace belongs to neither name nor value
an attribute-only header names no cookie
a header with no = at all names no cookie
an unnamed cookie is not a cookie
a nameless chunk is no boundary, so it stays inside the value before it
the same name set twice - both are reported, in wire order
